# nexus host add

Register a host and pin its certificate

Register a host. The server certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint is shown and must be
confirmed on the terminal or match --fingerprint; compare it with `nexusd tls fingerprint`
on the host. A certificate that verifies against system trust is trusted that way instead.
The token is read from the terminal without echo, or from stdin with --token-stdin;
it is never accepted as an argument.

## Usage

```
nexus host add NAME --url URL [--fingerprint SHA256] [--token-stdin] [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  nexus host add nas --url https://nas.lan:8443
  nexus host add nas --url https://nas.lan:8443 --fingerprint SHA256 --token-stdin < token.txt
```

## Flags

```
      --default              make this the default host
      --fingerprint string   expected SHA-256 fingerprint of the server certificate
  -h, --help                 help for add
      --tag strings          tag the host; repeat for more
      --token-stdin          read the token from stdin instead of prompting
      --url string           host URL, such as https://nas.lan:8443 (http:// only for a loopback IP)
```

## Global flags

```
      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
```
